title: Etaleness between smooth schemes is detected by the relative cotangent map
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $h:X\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism. Write $dh:h^*\Omega^1_{Y/S}\to\Omega^1_{X/S}$ for the map induced by $b\mapsto d(h^\#b)$, using relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every $x\in X$, $h$ is etale on some open neighbourhood of $x$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] if and only if the stalk $(dh)_x$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $h$ is etale if and only if $dh$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. If both differential sheaves are locally free of the same finite rank $d$, this is also equivalent to the determinant map $\bigwedge^d dh$ being an isomorphism everywhere [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]; for $d=0$ this determinant is the identity of the structure sheaf.

proof.text: First suppose $h$ is etale on an open $V$ containing $x$. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-localization-relative-differentials] to the square with top map $h|_V:V\to Y$ and bottom map $\mathrm{id}_S$. The latter is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] applied to the whole open $S$. The result identifies $(h|_V)^*\Omega^1_{Y/S}\to\Omega^1_{V/S}$ as an isomorphism. The same comparison for the open immersion $V\to X$ identifies this map with $dh|_V$: both send $1\otimes db$ to $d(h^\#b)$. Thus $(dh)_x$ is an isomorphism. This also proves that a globally etale $h$ has invertible $dh$.

source.place: Tag 04BX, lemma-sheaf-differentials-etale-localization; open immersions: morphisms.tex Tag 02GP, lemma-open-immersion-etale

proof.text: Conversely suppose $(dh)_x$ is invertible. By [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free], both relative differential sheaves are finite locally free. Tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] preserves finite local freeness directly: pull back a local basis on $Y$ to its inverse-image open on $X$, giving the same finite basis. Hence [lem-sc-finite-locally-free-stalk-iso-neighborhood] gives an open $U\ni x$ on which $dh$ is invertible. The open inclusion $U\to X$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; smooth source locality in [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] gives $U\to S$ smooth. By the open comparison [lem-sfb-etale-localization-relative-differentials], the restricted $dh$ is exactly the cotangent map for $h|_U$. Replace $X$ by $U$. We now have $dh$ invertible everywhere and $X\to S$ smooth. By [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation], $h$ is locally of finite presentation: $X\to S$ is so by smoothness, while $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type since finite presentation is in particular finite generation.

source.place: Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free; algebra.tex Tag 05GF, lemma-map-between-finitely-presented; Tag 02FV, lemma-finite-presentation-permanence

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] for schemes regarded as representable algebraic spaces. Its differential modules and pullbacks are on the small etale ringed topoi. The canonical comparison [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-relative-differentials-comparison] identifies them with the associated usual Zariski differential sheaves, respecting universal derivations. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies their tensor pullbacks with the associated Zariski tensor pullbacks. These comparisons carry the postcomposition action of $h$ to precomposition with $a_0^*dh$: on a generator $db$ the resulting derivation is $D(h^\#b)$. Consequently, for a first order thickening $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ with square-zero ideal $\mathcal J$ and an $S$-lift $a:T\to X$ of $a_0$, postcomposition on the sets of lifts is represented by the map $\operatorname{Hom}(a_0^*\Omega^1_{X/S},\mathcal J)\to\operatorname{Hom}(a_0^*h^*\Omega^1_{Y/S},\mathcal J)$ sending $E$ to $E\circ a_0^*dh$. It is bijective because $a_0^*dh$ has inverse $a_0^*((dh)^{-1})$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. This uses no cohomology-vanishing or global trivialization of the vector bundles.

source.place: Tags 04FG and 02H5, lemma-difference-derivation and lemma-action-by-derivations; more general space version: spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tags 0618, 0619 and 04D0; scheme comparison: Tag 04CS and descent.tex Tag 03LC

proof.text: Test $h$ against an arbitrary first order thickening $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ of affine schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] and maps $a_0:T_0\to X$, $b:T\to Y$ with $ha_0=bj$. Regard $T$ as an $S$-scheme through $b$. Smoothness of $X\to S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] gives an $S$-lift $a:T\to X$ of $a_0$. Under the bijection of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] centered at $ha$, the prescribed lift $b$ corresponds to $D=\delta_{ha}(b)$. Step 3 gives the unique correction $E=D\circ(a_0^*dh)^{-1}$ and hence a unique lift $a_E:T\to X$ with $\delta_a(a_E)=E$. Naturality yields $\delta_{ha}(ha_E)=E\circ a_0^*dh=D=\delta_{ha}(b)$, so injectivity of this bijection gives $ha_E=b$. Every lift over $Y$ is an $S$-lift of $a_0$, and the same bijection and invertible precomposition force its correction to be $E$. We have proved both existence and uniqueness for every test diagram. Apply [lem-sfb-lfp-unique-infinitesimal-lifts-etale], with local finite presentation from step 2, to conclude that $h$ is etale. Before replacing $X$ by $U$, this says $h$ is etale on a neighbourhood of $x$.

source.place: Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, existence of the initial lift; Tags 04FG and 02H5, correction by a derivation; Tags 02HG and 02HM, definition-formally-etale and lemma-etale-formally-etale

proof.text: If $dh$ is an isomorphism, steps 2--4 give an open etale neighbourhood of every point. These opens cover $X$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] makes $h$ etale globally. Together with step 1 this proves the sheaf-level equivalence. Equally, if every stalk of $dh$ is an isomorphism, step 2 supplies open inverses; they agree on overlaps because the inverse of a fixed map is unique, and the sheaf gluing axiom gives a global inverse. The empty scheme causes no exception: the empty open cover is permitted and its sheaf maps are uniquely invertible.

source.place: Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize, source-open locality, including the empty source

proof.text: For the determinant assertion, trivialize both finite locally free differential sheaves of rank $d$ and pull back the chosen basis from $Y$ using [def-pc-module-pullback]. The local matrix of $dh$ is square, say $A$. The alternating multilinear expansion in [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power] gives $\bigwedge^d dh(e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_d)=\det(A)(f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge f_d)$. Thus the determinant line map is invertible precisely when $\det(A)$ is a unit. In that case [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] supplies the two-sided inverse $\det(A)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(A)$ for $A$. Conversely an inverse of $dh$ induces an inverse on exterior powers, by applying the wedge map to both composition identities. Local inverses glue by uniqueness, so $dh$ is invertible if and only if its top exterior power is. For $d=0$ both bundles are zero locally, and the degree-zero exterior power of every map is the identity of $\mathcal O_X$ by the degree-zero construction. No positivity assumption on $d$ is used.

source.place: Tag 07DQ, lemma-matrix-left-inverse, adjugate identity; determinant formula is the elementary alternating expansion of the exterior-power construction

lean.statement: theorem smooth_cotangent_etale_criterion {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) [Smooth f] [Smooth g] (h : X ⟶ Y) (w : h ≫ g = f) : (∀ x : X, (∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Etale (U.ι ≫ h)) ↔ IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map (g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackMap h ≫ ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsCongr w).hom))) ∧ (Etale h ↔ IsIso (g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackMap h ≫ ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsCongr w).hom)) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, f.relativeDifferentials.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank d → g.relativeDifferentials.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank d → (Etale h ↔ IsIso (smoothCotangentDeterminantMap f g h w d))) ∧ ((Classical.choose (Modules.exteriorSheaf_zero_iso ((Modules.tensorPullback h).obj g.relativeDifferentials))).inv ≫ smoothCotangentDeterminantMap f g h w 0 ≫ (Classical.choose (Modules.exteriorSheaf_zero_iso f.relativeDifferentials)).hom = 𝟙 (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))
